advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Change `and last_event` to `and last_event is not None` in close_phase_values post_write_tail computation.
evidence: scripts/rebar_duration_probe.py:94: `post = invocation.end - last_event if invocation.end is not None and last_event else None`
last_event is selected via `next((value for value in (signature_at, status_at, verdict_at) if isinstance(value, (int, float))), None)` (line 86-93), so 0.0 is a legitimate selected value but falsy
advisory.finding: `post` (post_write_tail) uses the truthiness of `last_event` rather than an explicit None check: `post = invocation.end - last_event if invocation.end is not None and last_event else None`. If the last event timestamp is exactly 0 (a valid Unix epoch value, and one the synthetic/relative test fixtures could produce), the phase is silently dropped even though a real interval exists.
advisory.suggested_fix: post = invocation.end - last_event if invocation.end is not None and last_event is not None else None

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an audit counter for `wait` calls whose cell_id is not found in the cells map so dropped invocation linkages are observable rather than silent.
evidence: scripts/rebar_duration_probe_support.py:437-438: `cell = str(args.get("cell_id", ""))` then `wrapper = cells.get(cell, Wrapper("other"))`
No audit['...'] increment on the miss path, unlike other unparsed branches (e.g. audit['target_text_unparsed'], audit['multi_target_wrapper'])
advisory.finding: The `wait` tool branch silently degrades to a no-op `Wrapper("other")` when the referenced cell_id is absent from `cells`: `wrapper = cells.get(cell, Wrapper("other"))`. A yielded cell that was never registered (e.g. its yield output was on a line the parser skipped as malformed, or cell_id formatting mismatch) becomes invisible — the originating gate command's completion is never recorded, and there is no audit counter distinguishing 'cell matched' from 'cell miss'. This makes a dropped linkage indistinguishable from a genuinely unrelated wait.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document or audit the 4-hour phase-window truncation so late tracker events dropped from phase computation are observable.
evidence: scripts/rebar_duration_probe_support.py:558: `else event["timestamp"] + 4 * 3600`
_completion_phase_timestamps skips any event with `timestamp >= upper` (line 477) with no audit trace
advisory.finding: In load_tracker, when an event is a repeated close for the same ticket and `config.until` is None, the fallback upper bound for the LAST close is `event["timestamp"] + 4 * 3600` (4 hours). A completion whose STATUS/SIGNATURE tracker events land more than 4h after the verdict will have status_at/signature_at silently dropped, producing understated verdict_to_status / status_to_signature phase durations without any indication the window truncated them.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-text grep in test_source_has_no_literal_machine_specific_path with a behavioral assertion (e.g. that DEFAULT_LOG_ROOTS resolve relative to Path.home() rather than a hard-coded machine path).
evidence: def test_source_has_no_literal_machine_specific_path() -> None:
sources = (Path(probe.__file__).read_text(), Path(probe.support.__file__).read_text())
assert all("/Users/" not in source for source in sources)
assert all("agent-force-guidance" not in source for source in sources)
The grepped artifacts are the executable Python modules under test, so the Rule-5 non-executable-instruction-artifact exception does not apply.
advisory.finding: test_source_has_no_literal_machine_specific_path asserts on the raw TEXT of the source files under test (probe.__file__ / probe.support.__file__), grepping for '/Users/' and 'agent-force-guidance'. This is source-grepping: it tests the implementation text, not observable behavior, and breaks on any behavior-preserving edit that mentions those strings (e.g. a docstring or comment) while catching no functional regression.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert the observable configuration instead: e.g. assert str(probe.DEFAULT_LOG_ROOTS[0]).startswith(str(Path.home())) and confirm the default tracker is a relative Path('.tickets-tracker'), rather than grepping source text.

evidence: def kaplan_meier_quantiles(items: list[Invocation]) -> dict[str, float | None]:
survival *= 1 - deaths / at_risk
if targets[quantile] is None and 1 - survival >= quantile:

No test in tests/scripts/test_rebar_duration_probe.py references kaplan_meier_quantiles (searched file names: classify_command, parse_logs, percentile, cohort, close_phase_values, _completion_phase_timestamps).

Named violating input: items = [Invocation(observed 100s, exit_code=0/complete), Invocation(observed 150s, exit_code=130/censored)] should exercise the deaths=1 then censored=1 branches and yield a p50 crossing at 100; no test drives it.
advisory.finding: The newly-added kaplan_meier_quantiles survival/censoring primitive (support.py:702) has no test. Its non-trivial death-vs-censor accounting and 1-survival >= quantile crossing logic is uncovered — a regression in the at_risk decrement or the censored/deaths split would go undetected.

No test references attach_events, resolve_target, or eligible_with_censoring.

advisory.finding: The added event-matching path (attach_events / resolve_target and its +/-3s time window and nearest-event selection, support.py) is untested. The window-boundary and nearest-anchor selection behavior — central to whether an invocation gets an event and thus enters the cohort — has no coverage.
